md_description: This workflow tracks the generation of induced pluripotent stem cell lines from skin fibroblasts, optional genetic enhancement of differentiation, and culture maintenance under defined conditions before measurement of reprogramming efficiency, differentiation potential, and cardiomyocyte function. The resulting data are integrated into a metadata table for comparing variability across cell lines and identifying predictors of successful cardiomyocyte differentiation.

skin_fibroblast_population.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I only included intrinsic origin/identity fields for the starting skin fibroblast population. I excluded any reprogramming, genetic modification, culture, capture, signal, or derived-table fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. Since no fields were already_generated, there was no need to suppress overlaps. The selected fields support identifying the donor/source material, its tissue origin, and any baseline donor-level descriptors needed to interpret later iPSC reprogramming outcomes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the human donor/source of the starting skin fibroblast population; use a stable string such as 'DONOR_001'. This is recorded once for the originating biological material and should not be repeated on downstream process or measurement nodes.
Anatomic source tissue for the starting somatic cells used for reprogramming. For this workflow the expected value is skin, typically recorded at the sample level before any reprogramming begins.
Baseline cell identity of the starting material prior to reprogramming, recorded as the source somatic cell type. In this workflow it should denote dermal fibroblasts or skin fibroblasts.
Biological species of the starting fibroblast population, recorded at sample registration before reprogramming. Use when comparing across model systems or human donors.

Free-text descriptor of the starting fibroblast source context, such as 'adult skin biopsy', 'neonatal skin biopsy', or 'commercial fibroblast line'. Record at the entity level before any manipulation.

reprogram_to_ipscs.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the reprogramming protocol parameters, reagent/agent details, and a key process-quality indicator. I excluded source fibroblast identity/origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded iPSC line properties, culture conditions, capture settings, raw files, and metadata table fields because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicates to suppress. The chosen fields are the minimum needed to reproduce and interpret the fibroblast-to-iPSC conversion step.

md_schema.descr: Method used to induce pluripotency in the fibroblast population, recorded at the process step before iPSC line creation. For this workflow it should indicate Yamanaka-factor-based reprogramming; use as a categorical process descriptor.

List or summary of the core reprogramming factors used during the conversion of fibroblasts to iPSCs, recorded at the time the process is performed. Typical Yamanaka factors are OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, and c-MYC; capture the exact factor set used in this experiment.

How the reprogramming factors were introduced into the fibroblasts during this process, such as viral transduction or episomal delivery. Record the active delivery strategy used to perform reprogramming.

Total duration of the reprogramming process in days, measured from factor introduction to emergence or collection of iPSC colonies. Typical values are on the order of days to weeks; record the actual duration used in this workflow.

Process output quality indicator measured after reprogramming, defined as the percentage of input fibroblasts or starting units that yielded iPSC colonies. Record as a percentage at the end of the reprogramming step; typical values may range from 0 to 100.

ipsc_lines.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the generated iPSC lines: line identity, genetic background, and pluripotency status/lineage context. I excluded reprogramming protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded culture-maintenance, genetic-editing, capture, raw-signal, and metadata-table fields because those are downstream nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so no field-name conflicts needed to be avoided. The fields are intended to let downstream users distinguish iPSC lines and understand their biological origin before optional modification and culture.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for each induced pluripotent stem cell line generated from the fibroblast reprogramming step; use a stable string such as 'iPSC_LINE_01'. This identifier is recorded once for the entity and should not be repeated on downstream process or measurement nodes.
Identifier linking the iPSC line back to the originating fibroblast donor/source material. Record at the iPSC entity level to preserve lineage across reprogramming; example format 'DONOR_001'.

Baseline genetic background of the line as inherited from the donor source, including strain, ancestry, or donor genotype context as relevant to the study. Record at the entity level before any optional genetic modification.

Intrinsic pluripotency designation of the cell line after successful reprogramming and prior to downstream differentiation. Use this to indicate whether the line is confirmed as pluripotent for later cardiomyocyte work.
Origin category of the iPSC line indicating that it was derived from skin fibroblasts in this workflow. Record once for the entity to document the starting lineage context.

apply_genetic_modifications.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only modification protocol details and process-level quality context: what type of edit was performed, how it was delivered, the target gene/construct, and whether the modification was successful. I excluded intrinsic iPSC line identity/genetic background because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded culture conditions, capture settings, raw signals, and derived-table fields because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicates to avoid. The fields are sufficient to reproduce the genetic enhancement step and interpret later differentiation outcomes.

md_schema.descr: Primary type of genetic modification applied to the iPSC lines during this process step, recorded before downstream culture or differentiation assays. Use to distinguish editing from transgene addition or related interventions.

Name of the target gene, locus, or introduced construct affected by the genetic modification, recorded at the time of the editing or transgene-introduction step. Examples include a specific cardiac regulator gene or an overexpression cassette.

Method used to deliver the genetic modification reagents into the iPSC lines during this process, such as electroporation or viral transduction. Record the active delivery strategy used for the edit or construct introduction.

Process-level success indicator for the genetic modification step, measured after editing or transgene introduction and before downstream culture. Record the percentage of treated cells or colonies that carried the intended modification; typical values range from 0 to 100.

modified_ipsc_lines.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the modified iPSC lines that reflect the resulting biological state after editing: line identity, modification status, and the modification carried. I excluded the upstream editing protocol details because those belong to the Process node, and I excluded culture conditions, measurement settings, raw signals, and derived-table fields because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlaps to suppress. The selected fields let downstream users distinguish unmodified from modified lines and interpret differentiation outcomes in light of the introduced changes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the genetically modified iPSC line; use a stable string such as 'MOD_iPSC_LINE_01'. Record at the entity level after modification and do not repeat this identifier on process or measurement nodes.

Boolean flag indicating whether the iPSC line carries an introduced genetic modification at this entity stage. Record true only for lines that have undergone the modification process in this workflow.

Categorical summary of the modification state of the iPSC line, recorded after the editing or transgene-introduction step and before culture maintenance. Use to distinguish successful modification from partial or absent modification.

Short description of the introduced edit, knockout, knockin, or transgene carried by the line, recorded as an entity property after modification. Example entries include the edited locus or construct name.

maintain_culture_conditions.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only culture-maintenance protocol parameters and process-level handling details that define how the iPSC lines were kept before assay. I excluded line identity and modification-status fields because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded instrument/capture, raw signal, and metadata-table fields because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no field conflicts to avoid. The selected fields capture the minimum reproducible culture context: medium, substrate, passage, timing, and maintenance conditions.

md_schema.descr: Culture medium used to maintain the iPSC lines during this process step, recorded at the time of maintenance before characterization. Include the exact medium formulation or a controlled categorical label if standardized across the experiment.

Cell culture substrate or surface coating used during iPSC maintenance, recorded at the process stage before assay. Examples include Matrigel, vitronectin, feeder layer, or gelatin depending on the workflow.

Passage number of the iPSC lines at the time culture maintenance conditions were recorded, measured immediately before downstream characterization. Typical values are integer passage counts reflecting expansion history.

Duration in hours that the iPSC lines were maintained under the recorded culture conditions prior to characterization or transfer, measured for this process step. Record the actual elapsed time used in the workflow.

Free-text notes capturing additional handled culture-maintenance parameters not covered by medium, substrate, or passage number, such as feeder-free status, split ratio, or replenishment schedule. Record only process-relevant details controlled during maintenance.

cultured_ipsc_lines.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the cultured iPSC lines that reflect their state after maintenance, not the maintenance protocol itself. I excluded culture-medium, substrate, passage, and timing details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded capture settings, raw files, and the metadata table because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicate-name or semantic-overlap constraints to resolve. The fields describe the cultured line identity, its current maintenance state, and its readiness/context for downstream characterization and differentiation assessment.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the iPSC line after culture maintenance, used to track the maintained entity into downstream characterization. Example format 'CULTURED_iPSC_LINE_01'. Record once at the entity level.

Intrinsic culture status of the line at the time it is handed off for characterization, indicating whether the line is actively maintained, expanded, or temporarily held. Record as an entity-level descriptor.

Qualitative assessment of the cultured line's health or condition at the entity stage before characterization, such as normal morphology or stressed/compromised state. Use this to capture the overall biological readiness of the culture.
Boolean flag indicating whether the cultured iPSC line is considered suitable for downstream characterization and differentiation assessment at the time of handoff.

characterize_ipsc_lines.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration details used to characterize the iPSC lines, plus active assay settings and instrument identity. I excluded sample/entity properties such as line identity, modification status, and culture conditions because those belong upstream, and I excluded raw file properties and interpreted outputs because those belong to the Signal and Derivative nodes downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so no conflicts had to be resolved. The resulting fields are sufficient to document how the characterization was performed and on which platform, without leaking signal- or result-level metadata.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the characterization instrument or phenotyping platform used for this measurement session, recorded as part of the actively configured capture environment. Example: a commercial instrument vendor name.
Model name or number of the instrument used to capture iPSC characterization readouts, recorded at the measurement-session level. Example format: 'Model X123'.
Serial number of the characterization instrument used for this capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware configuration. Example format: 'SN-000123'.

Type of assay or instrumental characterization performed on the iPSC lines during this capture session. Record the active measurement modality used to obtain reprogramming, differentiation, or cardiomyocyte function readouts.

Concise summary of the actively configured capture settings used during characterization, such as excitation/emission configuration, acquisition mode, or plate-reader parameters depending on assay type. Record the operator-controlled settings relevant to reproducing the measurement session.
Unique identifier for the characterization session or run, used to group measurements collected together on the same instrument setup. Example format 'CAPTURE_RUN_001'.

raw_characterization_signals.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw-data artefact properties: file format, size, dimensions, storage location, and basic technical quality indicators. I excluded instrument settings and assay context because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded interpreted reprogramming/differentiation readouts because those are not raw artefact properties and would belong to a Derivative node if computed. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlaps to avoid. The fields are enough for data ingestion, traceability, and basic technical assessment of the measurement files.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw characterization data file or object, recorded for the signal artefact after acquisition. Example format 'RAWFILE_001'.

Technical format of the raw characterization file as stored after acquisition, such as FASTQ, CSV, TIFF, or vendor-specific instrument output. Record the actual file encoding used for the raw artefact.
Size of the raw data file in bytes, measured after acquisition and before any downstream processing. Typical values depend on assay modality and may range from kilobytes to gigabytes.

Dimensionality summary of the raw signal artefact, such as number of rows and columns for tabular output or image frame dimensions for imaging-based assays, recorded for the stored file. Use a concise textual description like '1024x768' or '384_wells_x_10_timepoints'.
Storage location for the raw characterization artefact, recorded after acquisition for traceability and retrieval. Example format: a local path, object-store URI, or repository link.

Basic technical quality assessment of the raw signal file, such as whether acquisition was successful and the file is readable. This should reflect signal-level integrity rather than scientific interpretation.

assemble_metadata_table.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the table-assembly operation details: software used, key transformation settings, input/output join context, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded entity fields from cultured iPSC lines and raw signal file properties because those belong upstream, and I excluded the final table schema/content because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating likely prior fields from other nodes by keeping this focused on the assembly operation itself rather than re-stating source identifiers or capture metadata. The fields are sufficient to reproduce how the metadata table was built from upstream sources.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, package, or pipeline used to assemble the unified metadata table from upstream culture descriptors and raw characterization outputs. Record the tool that performed the process, for example a Python/pandas workflow or database ETL script.
Version of the software or package used for metadata-table assembly, recorded at the time the process is run. Include a semantic version or release tag when available, such as '1.5.2'.

Repository, codebase, or script location for the table-assembly workflow, recorded to support reproducibility of the process. Example formats include a Git URL, internal code path, or notebook identifier.

Description of the key fields or matching strategy used to merge raw characterization outputs with culture and line descriptors during table assembly. Record the process-level linking logic, such as line identifier plus session identifier.

Number of table records produced by the assembly process, measured after merging upstream inputs and before downstream use of the derivative table. This is a process output quality indicator and should be a non-negative integer.

ipsc_metadata_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result properties of the metadata table itself: table identity, schema/shape, derivation method, and quality/completeness indicators. I excluded raw file properties, capture settings, and process parameters because those belong to upstream Signal/Capture/Process nodes, and I did not repeat line identifiers or source descriptors because those were generated on earlier Entity nodes and the table is a computed summary rather than a primary sample record. No already_generated list was provided in this turn, but the fields were chosen to avoid overlapping with the obvious upstream entity/process fields. The result is a compact description of the assembled analysis table for downstream reuse and interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed iPSC metadata table, recorded for the final derivative artefact. Example format 'IPSC_META_TABLE_001'.
Storage or exchange format of the computed metadata table after assembly, such as CSV, TSV, Parquet, or database table. Record the actual output format of the derivative artefact.
Number of iPSC-line records contained in the computed metadata table, measured after assembly is complete. This is a derivative shape metric and should reflect the final table size.
Number of columns or metadata fields present in the computed table after integration of lineage, culture, and characterization descriptors. Record the final schema width of the derivative artefact.

Brief description of how the table was computed from upstream raw characterization outputs, cultured line descriptors, and assembly outputs. Include the main integration approach at the derivative level, not the process software details.
Percentage of missing values across the computed metadata table, measured after assembly and before downstream analysis. This is a derivative quality indicator typically ranging from 0 to 100.
